-## Measurement audit (done first, while free)
-- **No-holdout spec.** `splits.json` train == val == test (same 10 ids). The framework already
-  logged `splits_warning`. Every number this run produces is a FIT metric, not generalisation.
-- **No environment fault.** All 30 baseline rollouts have `errored_trials: 0`, `rollout.error is
-  None`, and no traceback / permission-denied / timeout / gateway error in any of the 30 traces.
-  The only stderr is a benign openpyxl `Data Validation extension is not supported` warning. So
-  every failure below is a capability failure and is mine to fix.
-- **Two tasks have a ceiling below 1.0 that no prompt can lift** (verified against the on-disk
-  answer workbooks):
-  - `52532` copy 3: the gold answer workbook stores live array formulas AND its own score grid
-    differs from the input's (Game 2: input 483, answer 383), which flips the winner. No
-    computation over the input can reach it. **2/3 = 0.667 is this task's ceiling.**
-  - `53449`: the gold writes the literal token `'X'` under header `'Test'`; neither string appears
-    in the instruction or the preview. The *shape* rule (sparse fill) is recoverable, the cell
-    CONTENT is not. Treated as near-zero-capped.
-- Per-task bands: 5 tasks at 3/3 (leave alone), `43213` at 2/3 = genuinely unstable, `52532` at
-  2/3 = deterministic ceiling not variance (identical `[1,1,0]` on all three trials), and
-  `47766 / 53449 / 56915 / 188-39` at 0/3 = real reproducible defects. Baseline val 0.5333.
-## Ranked issue list (leverage = tasks x trials x score recoverable)
-| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |

-| 1 | **verification has no pass/fail predicate** | 56915, 188-39, 47766, 43213(t1) | The agent DOES verify, then ignores what it sees. 56915 printed `Row 19: [None,None,None,None]` twice and shipped it. 188-39 "fixed" a pandas float-display artifact by forcing text. 47766 printed its own number back and re-sent identical code. Verification with no accept/reject criterion is decoration. | BEHAVIORAL (structure) | ordered procedure + explicit finish-gate (task_template) |

-| 2 | **scope/anchor blindness** | 47766 | Target K40 already held `14755` = the PE total of rows 8-37 ONLY. Agent printed it, wrote the hypothesis in a comment, then summed all three row-blocks (53605 / 20535). All 3 trials "HIGHER than expected", so no year choice can pass while scope spans 3 blocks — scope is the defect. | KNOWLEDGE (missing method) | worked-procedure rule: reproduce the anchor before extending it (prompt) |

-| 3 | **empty cell written where lookup source is blank** | 56915 | 16/24 cells numerically EXACT; the 8 misses are rows 19-20, section headers blank in DATA, so `cell.value = None`. Gold holds int `0` because Excel's `INDEX()` over a blank returns 0. One-line class of bug. | KNOWLEDGE | sourced rule: blank lookup source = 0 (prompt) |

-| 4 | **right value, wrong stored type** | 188-39 | `pd.read_excel(..., dtype={'Contact no': str})` put 6 correct ints in as text. Self-inflicted: trial t1 omitted the dtype and had NO textform bucket (21 diffs vs 27). Caused by a pandas display artifact (`7.768826e+09`) read as file corruption. | KNOWLEDGE | contract rule: numbers as numbers + verify with openpyxl not pandas (prompt) |

-| 5 | **over-fill of a conditional column** | 53449 | Instruction states a co-occurrence CONDITION ("both an Office Visit and a Covid Test on the same day") + a pivot-table framing; agent wrote a label into all 15 rows, gold fills 2. 13 cells "written past where the answer ends". | KNOWLEDGE | conditional-on-observable-predicate rule (prompt) |

-| 6 | **clobbering pre-entered values** | 52532 | Instruction: "I manually recorded the win count in column H … for instance, Tim won 3 times". `.fillna(0)` over the whole column overwrote H3 (1 -> 2). Recovers 1 of the 2 differing cells; the other is the unreachable ceiling. | KNOWLEDGE | additive narrowing rule (prompt) |

-| 7 | **wasted identical rounds** | all 10 | 49945 3x, 438-18 3x, 160-6 3x, 47766 2x re-sent byte-identical code. In 47766 it cemented a wrong answer on the last round it could have reconsidered. | BEHAVIORAL (structure) | prohibition + preceding symptom (both files) |
-## Changes made this round (one row per edit)
-| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |

-| 1, 7 | ordered procedure with the finish step as a precondition | `task_template.md` | Replaced the flat 3-item "in each round" list with Steps 1-4 INSPECT -> SOLVE -> VERIFY -> FINISH, where FINISH is licensed only by four checkable predicates read off the Step-3 print-out. General: the predicates are mechanical (non-empty / typed / untouched-outside / consistent-with-anchor), never task-specific. | Step 1 forbids writing in round 1 only; every passing task already had spare rounds (3-5 used of 5). |

-| 1 | DELETED unhelpful guidance | `task_template.md` | Removed the framing that a saved file ends the job, replaced with "a saved file proves nothing: a wrong value, a value stored as text, and a cell left empty all save perfectly". The adapter docstring names this exact line as encouraging the dominant failure. No constraint lost — the write requirement survives as Step 2. | No passing task relies on stopping early. |

-| 2 | positive recipe (method the agent lacked) | `prompt.md` | "A value already in answer_position is a worked example … reproduce it first … if you cannot, your source range is wrong — usually narrower than you assumed." Plus Step 1c: print EACH candidate block's subtotal separately. | Guarded by "blank or 0 is not an example" — 4 of 5 passers have blank targets. |

-| 2 | conflict resolution (added to keep the anchor rule from over-reaching) | `prompt.md` | "An explicit cell reference in the instruction is exact … adjust the COLUMN from the header; never widen or move the ROWS." | Directly protects 43213 — see verify line below. |

-| 3 | sourced rule | `prompt.md` | "A blank source cell in a lookup contributes 0, not blank" — stated as what the spreadsheet function itself returns, so it generalizes to any INDEX/MATCH/VLOOKUP/SUMIF transcription. | Fires only inside a lookup over a blank source; no passing task does a lookup. |

-| 4 | output contract + tool-choice rule | `prompt.md` | Numbers as int/float, dates as dates, never `dtype=str` / `str(...)`; verify with openpyxl because pandas prints reformat ints and turn `NA` into `NaN`. Worded to forbid re-typing, not to force conversion. | Explicit carve-out "copy a value straight through unchanged" protects 160-6's text dates. |

-| 5 | conditional on an observable predicate | `prompt.md` | Trigger is wording the agent can see in the instruction ("both X and Y", "where", "if", "flag", "mark") -> fill only qualifying rows. Plus: do not invent a category from a remark about the input. | No passing task's instruction contains a row-level condition. |

-| 6 | additive narrowing | `prompt.md` | "Do not recompute over values the instruction describes as already entered … keep the original." Trigger requires the instruction itself to say manual/existing/example. | No passing task's instruction says that. |

-| 7 | prohibition + the symptom that precedes it | both | "If the code block you are about to send differs from the last one only in its comments or variable names, you have already failed." | It removes only wasted rounds. |
-## Verify-the-fix (one line per edit; trace evidence -> what changes)

-- **47766 (anchor).** Trace msg 3 prints `Cell K40 value: 14755`; msg 4 comments `# Actually, let's look at the existing value in K40: 14755. 14755 is likely the sum of all "PE" regardless of date` — then it computed `total_pe_all` over all three blocks (144890) and never printed it. I confirmed 14755 == the PE sum of rows 8-37 alone and of no other block combination. Step 1c ("subtotal of EACH candidate block separately") makes the comparison it proposed and skipped a required print; the anchor rule makes matching it a precondition of writing. All 3 trials wrote a 3-block sum and all 3 read "HIGHER than expected", so the year was never the defect.

-- **56915 (blank->0).** Its own verification printed `Row 19: [None, None, None, None]` / `Row 20: [...]` TWICE and it spent the remaining round on a column-matching refactor. The 16 cells it filled match gold exactly; gold rows 19-20 hold int `0`. `= val if val is not None else 0` is the whole fix, and Step 4's first predicate makes a `None` in range disqualify finishing.

-- **188-39 (type).** Final block is `pd.read_excel(..., dtype={'Contact no': str})`; gold C is `int`. Trial t1 omitted that dtype and its feedback has no `textform` bucket — proving the dtype line is self-inflicted. It was added in reaction to a pandas print showing `7.768826e+09`, a float64 display artifact of a correct int cell. The openpyxl-not-pandas rule removes the false signal; the type rule removes the reaction.

-- **53449 (conditional fill).** `df['Visit Category'] = df.apply(lambda x: mapping.get(...), axis=1)` returns one value per row, guaranteeing all 15 filled; gold fills 2. Instruction says "both an Office Visit and a Covid Test on the same day" — a per-row condition — and asks for a pivot-usable structure. The predicate rule writes only qualifying rows. Honest caveat: gold's literal `'X'` is unreachable from the prompt, so this edit recovers shape, probably not score, on this task; it is kept because the class (over-fill past where the answer ends) is general and it is bounded.

-- **52532 (pre-entered).** `df.iloc[:, 7] = df.index.map(win_counts).fillna(0)` overwrote H3 from 1 to 2 on copy 3 while the instruction said column H was hand-recorded. The rule keeps the original. Ceiling is 2/3 regardless (copy 3's gold needs the answer file's own recalculated grid), so this edit protects the 0.667, it does not raise it.

-- **43213 (the SAFE check that mattered).** This is the one passing-ish task the anchor/header rules could flip, so I traced all 3 trials. t0/t2 (1.0) read column **B** literally, verified `B12: 0 / B13: 0 / B14: 0 / B15: 0`, recognised the degenerate zeros, switched the SOURCE COLUMN to A via the headers (`Col A is "Value", Col B is "Average"`) — exactly the header rule — and passed. t1 (0.0) did the same column switch BUT also moved the row bounds from A11 (the instruction's start) to A2 ("average of A2:A12"), giving values LOWER than expected on all 4 cells. So the 2/3 is caused by row-bound drift, not by the column choice. The added "explicit cell reference is exact — adjust the COLUMN, never widen or move the ROWS" clause targets exactly t1's error while preserving t0/t2's winning move. The anchor rule is inert here: B12:B15 is blank/0 in the input, and "blank or 0 is not an example" excludes it.
-## Blast radius per edit class (named passing tasks, checked in-trace)
-- **BOUNDED, all of them.** Every prompt rule is conditional on a predicate absent from the
-  passing traces: anchor (needs a non-empty non-zero target: 49945/160-6/168-17/438-18 blank),
-  blank->0 (needs a lookup: none), pre-entered (needs the instruction to say so: none),
-  conditional fill (needs condition wording: none), type (carve-out for copy-through).
-- **Deliberately NOT shipped — four rules the trace evidence refuted**, because each would flip
-  a passing task:
-  - "leave every other cell in answer_position at its original input value" — breaks **160-6**
-    and **168-17** (both are row-delete/shift tasks, so the target range MUST change), and
-    **438-18** (target rows 4-6 are blank in the input and must be filled). 4 of 5 passers.
-  - "if any cell in answer_position is empty, fix it" — false-alarms on **168-17**, whose
-    correct answer prints as an empty DataFrame body, and on **438-18**/**160-6**. I scoped the
-    non-empty predicate to *cells your own solution assigned a value to*, which is what 56915
-    needs and what these three do not trip.
-  - "write dates as datetime, never str" as a blanket rule — endangers **160-6**, whose graded
-    A6:L11 contains text-formatted dates (`2022/08/19`) that must stay text. Kept only as
-    "do not re-type a value you are copying through".
-  - "when ambiguous, prefer the narrowest reading" — would have broken **43213**, where the
-    narrow literal reading of "average of B11:B12" is precisely the all-zeros wrong answer.
-- Adapter mechanic confirmed for the ordered procedure: `run_target` sets `solution_code` only on
-  a round whose write CHANGES the graded file, so a trailing verify-only round never becomes the
-  replayed artifact (`168-17__seed__t1` demonstrates the fallback). Adding Steps 3-4 is therefore
-  safe against the 2/3-copy replay. `VERIFY_TURNS=3` past the first write, `MAX_TURNS=5`.
-## Process & features used
-- Three read-only diagnoser subagents in parallel, one per trajectory group (53449+52532 /
-  56915+188-39 / 47766+all five passers), each ordered to quote code lines rather than summarize.
-  They independently recovered the on-disk gold workbooks, which is what turned two clusters from
-  guesses into measured ceilings. Merged serially into this one candidate.
-- Prior iterations: NONE exist (`prior_iterations/` absent, LEDGER has baseline only,
-  `rejected.jsonl` absent). Nothing to build on or avoid yet.
-- Placeholder contract checked before spending a rollout: `_task_template_error()` -> `None`, all
-  6 required placeholders present, `{max_turns}` kept, render test passes.
-## Good things to PRESERVE
-- The header-over-prose rule: it is 43213's and 56915's winning behaviour, not a new idea.
-- The "explicit cell reference is exact" clause paired with it — without the pair, the header rule
-  alone reproduces 43213 t1's row drift.
-- The copy-through carve-out on the type rule (protects 160-6's text dates).
-- Step 1's "do not write output_path in this round" — it is what converts round 1 from a blind
-  write (53449 wrote on turn 1 and never learned anything in 5 rounds) into evidence.
-## Deliberately skipped
-- `53449` cell CONTENT (`'X'` / header `'Test'`): not derivable from the instruction or preview.
-  Shape fixed, content conceded.
-- `52532` copy 3: gold needs the answer workbook's own recalculated score grid. Ceiling 0.667.
-- The five 3/3 tasks: noise-free passes, nothing to gain, everything to lose.

- You are a spreadsheet expert who can manipulate spreadsheets through Python code.
--Solve the given spreadsheet manipulation question precisely:

-+Your answer is graded by re-opening the file you saved at output_path and comparing the cells in answer_position against a reference workbook, one cell at a time. A cell matches only if BOTH its value and its stored type match. Prose you write is never graded — only the saved file.
-+## Read the evidence in the workbook before deciding what to compute
- - Read the instruction, spreadsheet content preview, instruction type, and answer position carefully before writing any code.

-+- **A value already sitting in answer_position in the INPUT file is a worked example of the expected answer.** If a target cell already holds a non-empty, non-zero value, that value pins down the SOURCE RANGE of the calculation. Reproduce it with your own logic first, print your reproduction beside it, and only then apply the extra condition the instruction asks for. If your logic cannot reproduce it, your source range is wrong — it is usually narrower than you assumed (one block of rows near the target cell, not every similar block in the sheet). Do not write a new value into a target cell while your own logic disagrees with the value that was already there. A blank or 0 cell is not an example; ignore it.

-+- **Let the target column's own header decide what that column holds.** Before choosing what to put in a column of answer_position, print that column's header cell in the TARGET sheet. When the header and the instruction's prose disagree about WHICH column supplies the numbers, the header wins: the person writing the instruction describes their sheet loosely, while the header is the sheet's own label.

-+- **But an explicit cell reference in the instruction is exact.** When the instruction names cells or a range ("X12 should contain the average of X11:X12"), those row numbers are the literal row bounds — start and end them exactly where the instruction says, even when the header tells you to read a different column. Adjust the COLUMN from the header; never widen or move the ROWS.

-+- **Do not recompute over values the instruction describes as already entered.** When the instruction says values were recorded manually, already exist, or offers one as an example, those cells are part of the specification: compute only the cells that are empty, and if your computed value disagrees with one that was already there, print both and keep the original.
-+## Write only what is asked, in the type the grader compares
- - For Cell-Level Manipulation questions, modify or fill in values ONLY within the exact cell(s) given in answer_position.
- - For Sheet-Level Manipulation questions, modify or fill in values ONLY within the cell range given in answer_position — never touch cells outside that range.
- - Prefer computing and writing LITERAL values (e.g. with pandas/openpyxl) over live spreadsheet formulas, so the result is unambiguous when the file is re-opened for grading.

-+- **Write a numeric result as a number** (int/float), and a date as a real date. Never write a number's text form. Do NOT read a column with `dtype=str`, and do not wrap a value in `str(...)`, to tidy up how it prints — the grader counts a right value in the wrong storage type as a miss. When you are copying a value straight through from the input, copy it unchanged rather than re-typing it.

-+- **A blank source cell in a lookup contributes 0, not blank.** When you are reproducing what a spreadsheet function would return (INDEX/MATCH, VLOOKUP, SUMIF, SUM) and the source cell you read is empty, the spreadsheet's own function yields 0 for a numeric column — write 0. Assigning `None` leaves the graded cell empty, and an empty cell never matches a cell the reference fills.

-+- **When the instruction describes a condition a row may or may not meet** (wording like "both X and Y on the same day", "where", "if", "flag", "mark"), write a value ONLY into the rows that satisfy it and leave the rest of answer_position untouched. Do not emit a label for a non-qualifying row, and do not invent an output category out of a remark about the input data (e.g. "some entries might be 'Not Specified'" describes the input, it is not a value to write).
-+## Make every round of execution tell you something
-+- **Every code block must `print(...)` something.** A block whose result comes back as "[Code executed successfully with no output]" has taught you nothing and has spent one of your limited rounds.

-+- **Verify by re-opening output_path with openpyxl — not with pandas.** A pandas print reformats integers as floats or scientific notation and silently turns a literal like `NA` into `NaN`, so a defect you "fix" on the strength of a pandas print is a fix to a display artifact rather than to your file. Print each target cell's value AND its type:
-+```python
-+from openpyxl import load_workbook
-+ws = load_workbook(output_path, data_only=True)["<sheet named in answer_position>"]
-+for row in ws["<the exact answer_position range>"]:
-+    for c in row:
-+        print(c.coordinate, repr(c.value), type(c.value).__name__)

-+- **A cell you wrote that prints as `None` is the defect, not noise.** If your code assigned a target cell a value and it came back `None`, fix that assignment — do not spend the round rewriting a part of the code that was already correct.

-+- **If the code block you are about to send differs from the last one only in its comments or variable names, you have already failed** — that round cannot change the graded file. Change the logic, or stop.
-+- If code execution returns an error, read the traceback carefully and fix the code — do not repeat a failing approach unchanged.
- - Always save your result to the exact output_path given, creating any missing parent directories first.

+## How to work
+You have up to {max_turns} rounds of interaction. Reply with exactly ONE python code block per
+round; its execution result comes back to you. Work through these steps IN ORDER — each one
+is a precondition of the next, so do not skip ahead to writing the file.
+**Step 1 — INSPECT (always your first round; never skip it).** Do not write output_path in this
+round. With openpyxl, print all of the following from the input file and read the results before
+you write any solution code:
+   a. the values currently in the cells of answer_position, with their types — this tells you
+      whether the target is blank, partly pre-filled, or already holds a worked example;
+   b. the header cell of every column that answer_position covers, in the TARGET sheet;
+   c. the candidate SOURCE cells your calculation would read, and — if your calculation
+      aggregates a block of rows — the subtotal of EACH candidate block separately, so you can
+      see which one matches a value already present in the target.
+   Base your solution on what these prints actually say, not on what you expected them to say.
+**Step 2 — SOLVE.** Write the modified workbook to output_path. Preserve everything the
+instruction does not ask you to change.
+**Step 3 — VERIFY (required; you are NOT finished when the file merely exists).** A saved file
+proves nothing: a wrong value, a value stored as text, and a cell left empty all save perfectly.
+Re-open output_path with openpyxl and print every cell of answer_position as
+`coordinate, repr(value), type(value).__name__`.
+**Step 4 — FINISH.** Reply with NO code block, and in that reply state the values you wrote.
+You may only do this once all four of these are true of the Step 3 print-out:
+   - every cell your solution was supposed to fill reads back non-empty (a cell that reads
+     `None` where your code assigned a value is a defect to fix, not noise);
+   - every number reads back as `int`/`float` and every date as a date — not as `str`;
+   - no cell outside the part of answer_position the instruction asks you to change was
